description: Representative async propagation, synchronous boundaries, runtime context, React compatibility, and error-shape cases.

cases.prompt: Migrate imports/api/invoices.js to Meteor 3. Follow the complete caller chain instead of changing only the Mongo call. Preserve the method boundary and existing return shape.

assertions.text: The Mongo read uses findOneAsync instead of synchronous findOne.
The order Promise is resolved before code reads the total property.
Promise handling propagates through calculateTotal and buildInvoice to the method boundary.
The method still resolves to an invoice object with a total field.

cases.prompt: A Meteor 2 class constructor assigns Orders.findOne(orderId) to this.order. Explain and show how to migrate it to Meteor 3 while preserving correct construction.

assertions.text: The answer does not declare or describe an async JavaScript constructor.
The answer awaits findOneAsync in an async factory or before passing a preloaded order.
The resulting constructor receives resolved data and remains synchronous.

cases.prompt: A package wraps Meteor.publish registration with EnvironmentVariable.withValue, but the value disappears after await inside the publication on Meteor 3. Diagnose the scope error and provide the correct wrapper boundary.

assertions.text: The actual publication handler invocation is wrapped instead of only its registration.
The withValue callback result is returned through the wrapper.
The proposed verification reads the environment value before and after an await.

cases.prompt: During a Meteor 3 React migration, must every component replace classic meteor/react-meteor-data hooks with the /suspense import? Include the package-version checks and boundaries that control the choice.

assertions.text: The answer states that classic reactive hooks remain supported.
The suspense path is conditional and requires an upstream Suspense boundary.
The answer identifies Suspense support in react-meteor-data 2.7.0 and Meteor 3 compatibility in 3.0.0.
The answer does not convert reactive client Minimongo reads to async reads by default.

cases.prompt: After migrating to callAsync, a client stub throws TypeError and the catch block crashes while reading error.error. Explain the possible rejection shapes and show safe narrowing without hiding intentional server failures.

assertions.text: The answer does not assume every local, misuse, or transport rejection is Meteor.Error.
The caught value is narrowed before reading error, reason, or details fields.
Intentional server-visible failures continue to use Meteor.Error.
